prompt: A square patio tile is $12$ in on each side. A quarter circle with radius $12$ in is drawn with its center at one corner of the tile, and that quarter circle is painted blue. How many square inches of the tile stay unpainted? Round to the nearest tenth.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller: a $2$ by $2$ square with a quarter circle of radius $2$ leaves $4 - \frac{1}{4}\pi(2)^2 = 4 - \pi \approx 0.9$ sq in unpainted. Same subtraction, bigger numbers.

explanation: The whole tile is $12 \times 12 = 144$ square inches.
The blue region is one quarter of a circle of radius $12$: $\frac{1}{4}\pi(12)^2 = \frac{1}{4}(144\pi) = 36\pi \approx 113.1$ sq in.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sensible-size check
steps: A quarter circle of radius $12$ drawn from a corner of a $12$-inch square fills most of the tile, leaving only the far corner region.
So the leftover must be well under half of $144$ — about $31$ sq in, roughly a fifth of the tile.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Choice C, $113.1$, is the painted quarter circle itself — a correct calculation of the wrong region, since the question asks for what is left UNPAINTED. Choice B comes from taking a quarter of the radius instead of a quarter of the area.
Underline what the question asks for before computing, and finish by asking "did I subtract?" Here the last move must be $144 - 113.1$.
